paragraphs: Teacher Kim has an idea for a new game. It is called "Who Is It?" We think of someone and write a card about the person. Then the children guess. They must say the name. Here is my first card. This man is about thirty years old. He is tall and strong. His hair is black and short. His eyes are brown. He wears a red shirt and black shorts. A whistle is around his neck. He is loud, too. Who is it?

Here is my second card. This man is older, and he is not tall. He has round glasses and a big white mustache. He has no hair on top. He has white hair next to his ears. He wears a green sweater and brown trousers. He takes his glasses off when he reads. Sometimes he buys ice cream for us. Who is it?

My third card is not about a person. This one is a small puppy. He is brown and small, and he has long ears. His nose is black, and he has a happy face. He wears a red collar. He runs better than any child in our street. Now the children guess. "Card one is Coach Matt!" says Leo. "Card two is Grandpa," says Mia. "He has a funny mustache!" she adds. "Card three is Pip!" all the children shout. They are all right, and I smile at my friends.
text.summary: Teacher Kim's class plays a guessing game. Lily writes three cards about Coach Matt, Grandpa, and Pip, and her friends guess who they are.
